processGame.name: Process a full game
processGame.description: Create a function called processGame that takes a target word and an array of guesses, and calls colorRow for each guess with the correct states.

duplicateLetters.name: Bonus: Handle duplicate letters
duplicateLetters.description: There's one Wordle rule we've skipped over. If a letter appears twice in your guess but only once in the target word, then if either one is in the right place, that one goes green and the other goes gray. Otherwise the first goes yellow and the second goes gray. The same idea scales up: three in a guess and two in the word means two get colored and the third goes gray. Start with the first bonus scenario, then fully solve it for the second. It's a bonus, so you don't have to complete it!

holeInOne.name: First time!
holeInOne.description: Deal with a first correct guess.

bonus1.name: Only one yellow
bonus1.description: If there are multiple present letters for only one actual letter, only one should be yellow.

bonus2.name: Swiss Cheese
bonus2.description: The swiss in this shows why it's important!

reuseWork.question: How do I reuse my work from `processGuess`?
reuseWork.answer: The logic that turns one guess into an array of states is the same. Pull it into a helper function (or copy it) and call it for each guess in the array.

trackRow.question: How do I track which row each guess belongs to?
trackRow.answer: Loop through the guesses with an index. The row number is the index plus `1` (since `colorRow` expects rows numbered `1-6`).

colorRow.question: How do I actually color each row?
colorRow.answer: Once you have the `states` array for a guess, call `colorRow(rowNumber, states)`.

fewerGuesses.question: What if the player has made fewer than 6 guesses?
fewerGuesses.answer: Only color rows for the guesses that exist. The array length tells you how many to process, so you naturally stop at the right point.

colorRow.description: Colors a row on the Wordle board with the given states.
